label: copy-phase input "0" (fed-back output 0) near the end of short sequences
explanation: Fires almost exclusively (99.8% of mass) on copy-phase steps whose input is the digit 0, i.e. the step right after the model has output a 0 and it is fed back. Never fires in the original or delimiter phase, and essentially never on any other input token (including other digits). Among copy-phase 0 inputs it is gated by position: it fires when at most ~3 outputs remain and the sequence is short (L <= 6); 0 inputs early in long sequences (L >= 7, many outputs left) are mostly silent. Strongest activations (near max) are when the 0 was the first original token and is fed back at step L+1 in L = 3-4 sequences; magnitude is lowest for late/long-sequence 0 inputs. Residual misses are weak activations on 0 inputs with 4-5 outputs left; false positives are mostly 0 inputs at the final step of L = 6 sequences.

issues: The core claim holds. All activation is in the copy phase (share 1.000; the original and delimiter phases have 0 active steps), and in_tok == '0' carries 99.8% of the mass. Non-0 inputs account for 1.2% of active steps and 0.2% of mass, so that is scattered noise.

On the data, the predicate is identical to '(L<=5) | (L==6 & recall_idx>=2)'. The two give the same dev and test scores (P 0.832, R 0.838, F1 0.835 on test). So 'to_go<=3' only matters for L=6 and simply drops recall_idx 1.

'Near the end' is wrong for L>=6. Precision in each (L, recall_idx) cell for copy-phase 0 inputs: L=6 peaks mid-copy (r=3, to_go 2: 0.92; r=4: 0.79) and falls at the last step (r=5, to_go 0: 0.41). For L=7 it fires mid-copy (r=3: 0.45, r=4: 0.36) but hardly at the end (r=5: 0.12, r=6: 0.05). For L=8-9 the only weak firing is at r=3-4 (0.10-0.14). The behaviour is better described as a window of recall_idx of about 2-4 that shrinks and weakens as L grows. In L<=4 the window covers the whole copy phase, and L=5 r=1 is only partial (0.55).

The description of the misses is wrong. The largest class of missed activations is L=7 with to_go<=3: 9.2% of active steps, 2.5% of mass, at precision 0.25. The class the explanation names (L>=7 with 4-5 outputs left) holds only 3.3% of active steps and 0.7% of mass.
The description of the false positives is roughly right: the main ones are L=6 r=5 (59% silent), L=5 r=1 (45% silent) and L=6 r=2 (45% silent).

I found no hidden variable behind the cells that only partly fire. Split by number of prior 0s, previous token digit vs letter, previous token vowel or n_digits, the firing rate barely moves (for example L=6 r=5 is 0.39 vs 0.38 for 1 vs 3 prior 0s). It looks like a graded position effect cut off by the activation threshold. That caps F1 near 0.835 for every simple predicate I tried, so the predicate itself is acceptable.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input '0' (fed-back output 0) in short sequences, positionally gated: fires anywhere in the copy for L<=5 (strongest at the first copy steps of L=3-4), only mid-copy (recall_idx ~2-4) for L=6-7, and almost never for L>=8
